## `ultrafast`

### `plot(result, what: str = 'overview', ax = None)`

Quick matplotlib plots of a :class:`Result` or a CLI results folder ("overview", "measurements", "spectrum", "temporal", "phase", "losses", "elements"). Full reports: :func:`ultrafast.plotting.report`.

### `load(directory)`

Open a results folder written by the CLI (``summary.json`` + ``result.npz``) -- no engine needed.

## `ultrafast.core`

Running systems, results, commands (studies, retrieval, materials).

Pythonic wrapper over the C API: :class:`System`, :class:`Run`, :class:`Result`.

### class `UltrafastError(RuntimeError)`

An error reported by the engine (bad JSON, unknown model, failed run...).

* `__init__(code: int, message: str)`

### `version() -> str`

Engine version string.

### `capabilities() -> dict`

Built-in model kinds, element types, materials and instruments.

### `command(request: Mapping[str, Any]) -> dict`

Run a JSON command of the engine (``uf_command``): ``{"command": "study" | "retrieve" | "materials.list" | "materials.show" | "materials.import" | "devices" | "compute.default", ...}``. The higher-level :func:`study`, :func:`retrieve` and :mod:`ultrafast.materials` wrap it.

### `devices(selftest: bool = False, benchmark: bool = False, backend: Optional[str] = None, device: Optional[int] = None) -> dict`

Compute back-ends and devices (docs/reference/speed.md): ``{"defaultBackend", "fft", "backends": [...], "devices": [{"backend", "index", "name", "memoryBytes", "doublePrecision", "usable", ...}]}`` -- the CPU first, then CUDA / OpenCL devices found by the gpu plugin. ``selftest=True`` compares every usable device (or only ``backend`` / ``device``) with the CPU on standard problems (result in ``"selftest"``); ``benchmark=True`` also times both.

### `benchmark(backend: Optional[str] = None, device: Optional[int] = None) -> List[dict]`

Seconds per run on the CPU and on each device for growing 1-D and spatial problems, with the speed-up (``[{"problem", "n", "cpuSeconds", "deviceSeconds", "speedup", "relativeError", ...}]``; the first device of each available back-end unless ``backend`` / ``device`` are given). Takes a few minutes.

### `set_default_backend(backend: Optional[str] = None, fft: Optional[str] = None) -> dict`

Process-wide defaults: the back-end of runs whose spec has no ``compute.backend`` ("cpu", "auto", "cuda", "opencl"; None keeps the current one) and the CPU FFT provider ("auto", "managed", "fftw", "accelerate"). Returns the settings in force. The ULTRAFAST_BACKEND / ULTRAFAST_FFT environment variables set the initial values.

### `study(system: Any, run_spec: Any, parameters: Sequence[Mapping[str, Any]] = (), outputs: Sequence[str] = (), mode: str = 'scan', output: Optional[PathLike] = None, **options) -> dict`

Parameter study (docs/reference/studies.md): ``mode`` "scan" (``sampling`` grid | random | lhs | sobol, ``samples``), "optimize" (``objective={"output": ..., "goal": "min" | "max" | "target", "target": ...}``) or "sensitivity" (``sensitivity={"method": "local" | "sobol"}``) or "coherence" (``coherence={"trials": 10, "at": "end"}``: repeated runs with independent quantum noise, result in ``analysis["coherence"]``). Parameters are ``{"path": "element:ID/key", "min", "max"}``; outputs are names like ``"pulse:end/fwhmS"``, ``"record:plate/BIntegralRad"``, ``"instrument:ac/fwhmS"``. Returns the study result (rows, analysis); ``output`` also writes study.json / study.csv.

### `coherence(system: Any, run_spec: Any, trials: int = 10, at: str = 'end', parallel: int = 4, seed: int = 1, output: Optional[PathLike] = None) -> dict`

First-order spectral coherence |g12(lambda)| over ``trials`` runs with independent one-photon-per-mode noise (docs/reference/fibers.md#noise-and-coherence). Returns ``{"meanCoherence", "wavelength_m", "g12", "spectrum", ...}``.

### `retrieve(method: str, trace: Any, kind: Optional[str] = None, fundamental: Optional[PathLike] = None, material: Optional[str] = None, output: Optional[PathLike] = None, energy: float = 1e-09, instrument: Optional[str] = None, **options) -> dict`

Pulse retrieval (docs/reference/retrieval.md): ``method`` "pcgpa" | "epie" (FROG) or "dscan"; ``trace`` an NPZ / JSON file or a dict of arrays (delay_s or insertion_m, omega_rad_s or wavelength_m, trace). A results folder's ``result.npz`` works too: ``instrument`` names the frog / dscan instrument when there are several. Returns the result with a ready-to-use run-spec ``"pulse"`` (the retrieved spectrum and phase).

### class `Run(_Handle)`

A system + a run spec (+ callbacks). Call :meth:`execute` to propagate.

* `__init__(system: System, spec: JsonLike)`
* `time_response(name: str, fn: Callable[[ResponseContext], Any], carrier_resolved: bool = False) -> 'Run'` -- Register a Delta n(t) model under ``name``; reference it from the run spec / system file as ``{"kind": "callback", "name": name}`` (e.g. an override with ``"property": "timeResponse"``). ``fn(ctx)`` may write ``ctx.dn_re`` / ``ctx.dn_im`` in place, or return ``dn_re`` or ``(dn_re, dn_im)``.
* `index(name: str, fn: Callable[[np.ndarray], np.ndarray]) -> 'Run'` -- Register n(omega) under ``name`` (use as a material ``"index": "@name"``).
* `field(name: str, fn: Callable[[np.ndarray, np.ndarray, np.ndarray], np.ndarray]) -> 'Run'` -- Register a position-dependent property f(x, y, z) (arrays in m, x/y from the beam axis, z from the element start) -> values; use it as ``"indexProfile": "@name"``, ``"absorptionProfile": "@name"``, ``"n2Scale": "@name"`` or in gain media (docs/reference/spatial-properties.md).
* `filter(name: str, fn: Callable[[np.ndarray], Union[np.ndarray, Tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]]]) -> 'Run'` -- Register a spectral filter: ``fn(omega) -> T`` or ``(T, phase)`` (power transmission, rad).
* `beam(name: str, fn: Callable[[np.ndarray], Union[np.ndarray, Tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]]]) -> 'Run'` -- Register a beam model: ``fn(z) -> radius`` or ``(radius_x, radius_y)`` (1/e^2 radii, m).
* `array_function(name: str, fn: Callable[[np.ndarray], np.ndarray]) -> 'Run'` -- Register a generic y = f(x) (e.g. a Raman response h(t), or attenuation via ``name + '#index'``).
* `element(name: str, fn: Callable[['ElementContext'], Any]) -> 'Run'` -- Register a user element under ``name``; use it as ``{"type": "user", "callback": "@name", "params": {...}}``. ``fn(ctx)`` returns ``(ax, ay)``, ``ax``, or None (see :class:`ElementContext`).
* `execute(progress: Optional[Callable[[str, int, int, float], Optional[bool]]] = None) -> 'Result'` -- Propagate. ``progress(element_id, index, count, fraction)`` may return True to cancel.

### `run(system: Union[System, JsonLike], spec: JsonLike, callbacks: Optional[Mapping[str, Any]] = None, progress = None, elements: Optional[Mapping[str, Any]] = None, fields: Optional[Mapping[str, Any]] = None) -> Result`

One-call simulation. ``callbacks``: {"name": function} time responses (take a ResponseContext); ``elements``: {"name": function} user elements (take an ElementContext); ``fields``: {"name": f(x, y, z)} position-dependent properties. ## `ultrafast.build`

Builders for system files and run specs (`from ultrafast import build as b`).

Helpers to write system files and run specs from Python (plain dicts, so they can be inspected, edited, saved with :func:`save` and versioned). Every helper simply returns the JSON the engine reads; see docs/reference/system-file.md and docs/reference/run-spec.md for all fields.

### `system(name: str, elements: Sequence[Mapping[str, Any]], materials: Optional[Mapping[str, Any]] = None, coatings: Optional[Mapping[str, Any]] = None, wavelengths_m: Optional[Sequence[float]] = None, overrides: Optional[list] = None, environment: Optional[Mapping[str, Any]] = None, description: Optional[str] = None, substrates: Optional[Mapping[str, Any]] = None) -> 'T.System'`

A system file. ``substrates`` defines mirror substrates by name (see :func:`substrate`); ``environment`` is the lab air (:func:`environment`).

### `bulk(id: str, material: str, length_m: float, beam: Optional[Mapping[str, Any]] = None, nonlinear: Optional[bool] = None, **extra) -> 'T.BulkElement'`

### `fiber(id: str, length_m: float, betas: Optional[Sequence[float]] = None, gamma: Any = None, *, betas_ps_km: Optional[Sequence[float]] = None, loss_db_per_km: Optional[float] = None, gain_db_per_m: Optional[float] = None, raman: Any = None, **extra) -> 'T.FiberElement'`

Single-mode fibre (docs/reference/fibers.md): Taylor ``betas`` [beta2, beta3, ...] in s^k/m (or ``betas_ps_km`` in ps^k/km), ``gamma`` in 1/(W m) (or an expression in z), loss, gain, ``raman`` = "silica" | "linAgrawal" | "hollenbeck" | "none". ``extra``: ``dispersion``, ``material``, ``n2``, ``effectiveAreaM2``, ``gain`` (spectrum), ...

### `gap(id: str, length_m: float, medium: str = 'Air', air: Optional[Mapping[str, Any]] = None, **extra) -> 'T.GapElement'`

Free space (air by default). ``air`` (see :func:`air`) gives this gap its own temperature, pressure, humidity or gas lines instead of the system's ``environment.air``.

### `interface(id: str, before: str = 'Air', after: str = 'Air', aoi_deg: float = 0.0, coating = None, mode: str = 'refract', **extra) -> 'T.InterfaceElement'`

### `mirror(id: str, coating = None, aoi_deg: float = 0.0, medium: str = 'Air', substrate: Any = None, ripple: Optional[Mapping[str, Any]] = None, delayed_scatter: Optional[Mapping[str, Any]] = None, **extra) -> 'T.MirrorElement'`

A reflecting surface. ``substrate``: a name ("FS-12.7mm", or one defined with ``system(substrates=...)``) or :func:`substrate` -- light leaking through the coating returns as an echo delayed by 2 n_g d cos(theta) / c. ``ripple``: :func:`coating_ripple`. ``delayed_scatter``: :func:`delayed_scatter`. ``aoi_deg`` defaults to 0 (a Herriott cell: a few mrad).

### `dispersion(id: str, gdd_s2: float = 0.0, tod_s3: float = 0.0, fod_s4: float = 0.0, **extra) -> 'T.DispersionElement'`

### `grating_pair(id: str, lines_per_mm: float, aoi_deg: float, separation_m: float, order: int = -1, passes: int = 2, efficiency: float = 1.0) -> 'T.GratingPairElement'`

### `chirped_mirror(id: str, gdd_s2: float, bounces: int = 1, reflectance: float = 0.999, tod_s3: float = 0.0, **extra) -> 'T.ChirpedMirrorElement'`

Dispersive mirror (GDD/TOD per bounce). ``extra``: e.g. ``rippleGddFs2=30, ripplePeriodNm=25, complementaryPairs=True``.

### `aperture(id: str, radius_m: Optional[float] = None, beam_radius_m: Optional[float] = None, *, half_width_x_m: Optional[float] = None, half_width_y_m: Optional[float] = None, decenter_x_m: Optional[float] = None, decenter_y_m: Optional[float] = None) -> 'T.ApertureElement'`

A hard aperture: round (``radius_m``) or rectangular (``half_width_x_m``, ``half_width_y_m``), optionally decentred. On a carried transverse profile it masks the field (edge cells transmit their area fraction) and the light diffracts in the spatial elements after it (docs/reference/transverse.md#diffraction-and-apertures); without one it clips the beam model of radius ``beam_radius_m``.

### `grating(id: str, lines_per_mm: float, aoi_deg: float, order: int = -1, efficiency: Optional[float] = None, **extra) -> 'T.GratingElement'`

One diffraction grating. With the beam tracked (an ``inputBeam``) it disperses the beam: sin(theta_out) = sin(theta_in) + m lambda / period with signed angles in the unfolded beam (a second grating that undoes it has ``aoi_deg`` = the first's diffraction angle and the opposite order), anamorphic magnification, angular dispersion, pulse-front tilt, and the group-delay dispersion of the spatio-temporal couplings (docs/reference/components.md#spatio-temporal-couplings).

### `waveplate(id: str, plate: str = 'half', axis_deg: float = 0.0, design_wavelength_m: Optional[float] = None, *, material: Optional[str] = None, order: Optional[int] = None, thickness_m: Optional[float] = None, construction: Optional[str] = None, plate_thickness_m: Optional[float] = None) -> 'T.WaveplateElement'`

Waveplate: dispersionless design model, or with ``material`` (Quartz, MgF2, ...) a thick plate with full dispersion (multi-order ``order`` / ``thickness_m``, or ``construction="compound"`` zero-order).

### `plate(id: str, material: str, thickness_m: float, aoi_deg: float = 0.0, ghosts: Any = False, coating: Any = None, wedge_deg: float = 0.0, beam: Optional[Mapping[str, Any]] = None, delayed_scatter: Optional[Mapping[str, Any]] = None, **extra) -> 'T.PlateElement'`

Plane-parallel plate / window: surfaces, bulk (dispersion, nonlinearity with a beam), optional ghost replicas. The ghosts use the reflectance of ``coating`` at each wavelength (a ``table`` coating or a stack), not a flat value. ``delayed_scatter``: bulk back-scatter returned as delayed light (:func:`delayed_scatter`; the default delay is 0 .. 2 n_g d / c).

### `nd_filter(id: str, od: Any, kind: str = 'absorptive', material: Optional[str] = None, thickness_m: Optional[float] = None, wavelengths_m: Optional[Sequence[float]] = None, aoi_deg: float = 0.0, ghosts: Any = False, **extra) -> 'T.NdFilterElement'`

Neutral-density filter: OD (or OD per wavelength with ``wavelengths_m``), absorptive or reflective.

### `thin_film_polarizer(id: str, output: str = 'transmitted', axis_deg: float = 0.0, aoi_deg: float = 56.0, model: str = 'stack', **extra) -> 'T.ThinFilmPolarizerElement'`

Thin-film polariser (physical quarter-wave stack or ideal); ``output`` "transmitted" (p) or "reflected" (s).

### `faraday_rotator(id: str, rotation_deg: float = 45.0, material: Optional[str] = None, length_m: Optional[float] = None, **extra) -> 'T.FaradayRotatorElement'`

Faraday rotator (non-reciprocal, Verdet ~ 1/(lambda^2 - lambda0^2)); with a crystal ``material`` and ``length_m``.

### `wavefront(id: str, zernike_noll_waves: Optional[Sequence[float]] = None, radius_m: Optional[float] = None, random_rms_m: Optional[float] = None, correlation_length_m: Optional[float] = None, **extra) -> 'T.WavefrontElement'`

A wavefront error: Zernike terms (Noll order, waves) over ``radius_m`` and/or a random figure (cartesian grids).

### `substrate(material: str = 'FusedSilica', thickness_m: Optional[float] = None, *, back_reflectance: Optional[float] = None, back_coating: Any = None, wedge_deg: Optional[float] = None, orders: Optional[int] = None, beam_radius_m: Optional[float] = None) -> dict`

A mirror substrate (for ``mirror(substrate=...)`` or ``system(substrates={name: ...})``). Light that leaks through the HR coating reflects from the back face (bare Fresnel unless ``back_reflectance`` -- a flat power reflectance, e.g. 1e-3 for an AR coating -- or ``back_coating`` is given) and returns ``orders`` times as an echo delayed by 2 n_g(lambda) d cos(theta_t) / c. Built-in names: FS-3mm, FS-6.35mm, FS-9.5mm, FS-12.7mm, FS-25.4mm, BK7-6.35mm, BK7-12.7mm (fused silica / N-BK7, bare back face).

### `coating_ripple(phase_rms_rad: float = 0.0, amplitude_rms: float = 0.0, max_delay_s: float = 5e-12, *, seed: Optional[int] = None, components: Optional[int] = None) -> dict`

Random phase / amplitude ripple of a mirror coating (for ``mirror(ripple=...)``). The first-order pedestal holds a fraction ``phase_rms_rad`` squared of the energy within +-``max_delay_s`` of the pulse. Measured ripple: use a ``table`` coating.

### `delay_uniform(max_s: Optional[float] = None, min_s: float = 0.0) -> dict`

Delays uniform in [min_s, max_s] (default max: 2 n_g d cos(theta) / c of the plate, or of the mirror substrate).

### `delay_exponential(tau_s: float, max_s: Optional[float] = None) -> dict`

Delays with an exponential weight exp(-t / tau_s).

### `delay_table(delays_s: Sequence[float], weights: Sequence[float]) -> dict`

Delays from a table (weights are normalised).

### `delayed_scatter(fraction: Optional[float] = None, delay: Optional[Mapping[str, Any]] = None, spectral_exponent: Optional[float] = None, *, seed: Optional[int] = None, components: Optional[int] = None, model: Optional[str] = None, roughness_rms_m: Optional[float] = None, correlation_length_m: Optional[float] = None, beam_radius_m: Optional[float] = None, surfaces: Optional[int] = None) -> dict`

Scatter as delayed light, not loss. Generic model: ``fraction`` of the power returns incoherently after ``delay`` (:func:`delay_uniform`, :func:`delay_exponential`, :func:`delay_table`) with an intensity weight lambda^-``spectral_exponent``. Analytic surface model (``model="surface"``): rms roughness ``roughness_rms_m`` gives the total integrated scatter (4 pi sigma / lambda)^2 per surface; the share 1 - exp(-(l/w)^2) of it (correlation length l, beam radius w) stays in the mode and returns after ``delay`` (none: at once), the rest is lost (booked as scatter). ``surfaces`` defaults to 1 (mirror) / 2 (plate).

### `air(*, temperature_c: Optional[float] = None, pressure_pa: Optional[float] = None, humidity: Optional[float] = None, co2_ppm: Optional[float] = None, apply_to_gaps: Optional[bool] = None, kind: Optional[str] = None, **model) -> 'T.Air'`

Lab air (Ciddor index from temperature, pressure, relative humidity 0..1 and CO2), for ``environment(air=...)`` or one ``gap(air=...)``. ``apply_to_gaps=True`` uses it as the "Air" of every gap (off by default: existing results do not change). ``kind="hitran"`` (hitran plugin) adds line-by-line absorption and dispersion: see ``ultrafast_hitran.air``.

### `environment(air: Optional[Mapping[str, Any]] = None, index_reference: Optional[str] = None) -> 'T.Environment'`

The system's ``environment``: the lab air and whether quoted data are relative to "air" or "vacuum".

### `grid(*, n: Optional[int] = None, window_s: Optional[float] = None, window_ps: Optional[float] = None, auto: Optional[bool] = None, max_n: Optional[int] = None, snap_carrier: Optional[bool] = None, spectral_margin: Optional[float] = None, min_span_fraction: Optional[float] = None, min_points_per_fwhm: Optional[float] = None, satellite_level: Optional[float] = None, extend_for_satellites: Optional[bool] = None, strict: Optional[bool] = None, tail: Any = None) -> 'T.Grid'`

The time grid. ``tail=True`` (or :func:`tail_grid`) adds the delayed-light ledger: a second, long, linear grid with the same time step that carries ghosts, echoes, scatter and gas-line tails while the nonlinear solver stays on the small main grid. ``extend_for_satellites=True`` grows a manual window to hold the satellites; ``strict=True`` makes a wrapping satellite an error.

### `tail_grid(window_s: Optional[float] = None, warn_energy_fraction: Optional[float] = None, *, exact_steps: Optional[bool] = None, cross_phase: Optional[bool] = None) -> dict`

``grid(tail=tail_grid(window_s=2e-9))``: the long tail grid of the delayed-light ledger (default window: from the satellites, at least 8 x the main window). A warning is added when the tail holds more than ``warn_energy_fraction`` (0.01) of the energy. ``exact_steps=True`` takes the exact long-grid step for every linear element (default: smooth elements -- dispersion, flat loss, bare surfaces -- act on main and tail separately, much cheaper); ``cross_phase=False`` leaves out the first-order cross-phase of the tail by the main pulse in nonlinear elements.

### `detector_response(wavelengths_m: Sequence[float], values: Sequence[float]) -> dict`

A spectral response table (e.g. the quantum efficiency) for ``detector(response=...)``: linear in wavelength, held at the ends.

### `detector(*, calibration: Optional[float] = None, noise: Optional[float] = None, noise_floor: Optional[float] = None, dynamic_range_db: Optional[float] = None, saturation_level: Optional[float] = None, bit_depth: Optional[int] = None, response: Optional[Mapping[str, Any]] = None, counting: Optional[str] = None, seed: Optional[int] = None, preset: Optional[str] = None) -> 'T.Detector'`

The read-out of an instrument (``instrument(..., detector=detector(...))``). ``response`` (:func:`detector_response`) is the spectral response of a spectral instrument; ``counting="photons"`` converts the energy spectrum to photon counts first. ``preset`` names an entry of ``run_spec(detectors=...)`` (or a JSON file) that the other keys override.

### `detector_preset(*, instrument: Optional[Mapping[str, Any]] = None, detector: Optional[Mapping[str, Any]] = None) -> dict`

A reusable detector preset for ``run_spec(detectors={name: ...})``: ``instrument`` keys fill instrument parameters the instrument does not set (``saturationLevel``, ``segments`` from :func:`detector_segment`, ``noiseFloor``, ...); ``detector`` is the read-out. An instrument uses it with ``detector="name"``. Numbers are yours (a manual, a calibration): none are built in.

### `detector_segment(from_s: float, to_s: float, attenuation: float = 1.0, noise_floor: Optional[float] = None) -> dict`

One delay range of a cross-correlator scan measured through an attenuation (a power factor): for the instrument's ``segments=[...]`` (stitching) together with ``saturation_level``-style keys ``saturationLevel`` and ``noiseFloor``.

### `pedestal(kind: str, **params) -> dict`

A pedestal / contrast component for ``pulse(..., pedestal=[...])``: kind replica | prePulse | postPulse | ase | phaseNoise | exponential (docs/reference/run-spec.md#pedestal); parameters in the engine's spelling (``delayS``, ``relativeIntensity``, ``rmsRad``, ...).

### `transverse(model: str = 'radial', points: Optional[int] = None, radius_m: Optional[float] = None, nx: Optional[int] = None, ny: Optional[int] = None, half_width_m: Optional[float] = None, transport: Optional[str] = None, initial_profile: Optional[Mapping[str, Any]] = None, *, absorbing_boundary: Any = None, spectral_samples: Optional[int] = None, **extra) -> dict`

Transverse (spatial) model for an element: "radial" (Hankel) or "cartesian" (x-y FFT). ``absorbing_boundary`` (True, or {"widthFraction": 0.15}) absorbs light leaving the grid in linear elements instead of reflecting / wrapping it (booked as "grid boundary"); ``spectral_samples`` (48) is the number of frequencies at which the profile is stored -- fewer is faster for narrowband pulses.

### `initial_profile(kind: str = 'gaussian', *, order: Optional[int] = None, radius_m: Optional[float] = None, geometry: Optional[str] = None, radius_x_m: Optional[float] = None, radius_y_m: Optional[float] = None, radius_of_curvature_m: Optional[float] = None, ripple: Optional[Mapping[str, Any]] = None, noise: Optional[Mapping[str, Any]] = None, **extra) -> dict`

The field at the first spatial element (``transverse(initial_profile=...)``): "gaussian", "superGaussian" (``order``), "flatTop" (super-Gaussian of order 10) or "tophat" (hard edge). ``geometry`` "round" (default) or "square" (separable in x and y; cartesian grids). ``radius_m`` (or ``radius_x_m`` / ``radius_y_m``) is the 1/e^2 radius, or the edge radius / half-width of a tophat; it replaces the element's beam size, so no ``beam`` is needed. ``ripple`` / ``noise`` (cartesian grids) seed small-scale self-focusing: :func:`profile_ripple`, :func:`profile_noise`.

### `profile_ripple(period_m: float, relative_amplitude: float, angle_deg: float = 0.0, phase_rad: float = 0.0) -> dict`

A sinusoidal amplitude ripple a cos(2 pi (x cos t + y sin t) / period + phase) on the field: the Bespalov-Talanov seed. The ripple of the fluence is 2 a; with a plane wave of intensity I it grows as cosh(g z), g^2 = q (2 Delta - q), q = K^2 / 2k, Delta = k0 n2 I.

### `profile_noise(relative_amplitude_rms: float = 0.0, correlation_length_m: float = 5e-05, phase_rms_rad: float = 0.0, seed: int = 1, components: Optional[int] = None) -> dict`

Seeded smooth random amplitude (relative rms) and phase noise with the given correlation length: the seed of small-scale self-focusing. The element reports ``fluenceContrastIn`` / ``Out`` and ``smallScaleGain``.

### `aux_beam(role: str, pulse: Optional[Mapping[str, Any]] = None, *, from_results: Optional[str] = None, energy: Optional[float] = None, radius_m: Optional[float] = None, profile: str = 'gaussian', order: Optional[int] = None, delay_s: Any = 'auto', radius_of_curvature_m: Optional[float] = None) -> dict`

Auxiliary beam for a crystal: a pulse spec (see :func:`pulse`) or ``from_results`` (a results folder).

### `crystal(id: str, crystal: Any, length_m: float, process: str = 'shg', type: Optional[str] = None, *, cut: Any = 'auto', noncollinear: Any = None, qpm: Any = None, aux: Optional[list] = None, output: Optional[str] = None, main_role: Optional[str] = None, record: Optional[list] = None, beam: Optional[Mapping[str, Any]] = None, transverse: Optional[Mapping[str, Any]] = None, deff_pm_per_v: Optional[float] = None, seed_noise: Optional[bool] = None, temperature_c: Optional[float] = None, overlap: Any = None, chi3: Optional[bool] = None, **extra) -> 'T.CrystalElement'`

A chi(2) crystal element (docs/reference/crystals.md).

### `pump(kind: str = 'cw', wavelength_m: float = 9.4e-07, radius_m: float = 0.0005, power_w: Optional[float] = None, energy_j: Optional[float] = None, profile: str = 'tophat', order: Optional[int] = None, passes: int = 1, delay_s: Optional[float] = None) -> dict`

A pump for gain / amplifier elements: kind "cw" (power_w) or "pulsed" (energy_j, delay_s before the seed); profile "tophat" | "gaussian" | "superGaussian" (order); passes 2 = reflected back through the crystal.

### `gain(id: str, medium: Any, length_m: float, pump: Optional[Mapping[str, Any]] = None, inversion: Optional[Mapping[str, Any]] = None, beam: Optional[Mapping[str, Any]] = None, mode_radius_m: Optional[float] = None, transverse: Optional[Mapping[str, Any]] = None, thermal_lens: Any = None, slices: Optional[int] = None, steady_state: Any = None, **extra) -> 'T.GainElement'`

A pumped gain medium crossed once (docs/reference/gain.md). ``medium`` = "Yb:YAG" | "Ti:sapphire" | "Nd:YAG" or a gain-medium object ({"base": "Yb:YAG", "dopingDensityM3": ...} or a full definition); ``inversion`` = {"fraction": b} or {"smallSignalGain": G} instead of / on top of a pump; ``transverse`` for spatial gain.

### `thermal_lens(*, rod_radius_m: Optional[float] = None, heat_fraction: Optional[float] = None, apply: Optional[bool] = None, track: Optional[bool] = None, focal_length_m: Optional[float] = None) -> dict`

The thermal lens of a gain element (``gain(thermal_lens=...)``; docs/reference/gain.md#thermal-lens): heat = ``heat_fraction`` (default the quantum defect) x absorbed pump, conducted to a rod of radius ``rod_radius_m``. ``track`` (default True) also puts it on the tracked Gaussian beam (thin lenses per slice, fitted over the beam); ``focal_length_m`` is a measured focal length used instead of the heat model.

### `multipass_amplifier(id: str, medium: Any, length_m: float, passes: int, pump: Optional[Mapping[str, Any]] = None, between_passes: Optional[Mapping[str, Any]] = None, mode_radius_m: Optional[float] = None, beam: Optional[Mapping[str, Any]] = None, inversion: Optional[Mapping[str, Any]] = None, **extra) -> dict`

A multipass amplifier (1-D): ``between_passes`` = {"loss": 0.02, "gddFs2": .., "materials": [{"name", "lengthM"}]}.

### `regenerative_amplifier(id: str, medium: Any, length_m: float, round_trips: Any = 'auto', pump: Optional[Mapping[str, Any]] = None, cavity: Optional[Mapping[str, Any]] = None, mode_radius_m: Optional[float] = None, beam: Optional[Mapping[str, Any]] = None, inversion: Optional[Mapping[str, Any]] = None, passes_per_round_trip: Optional[int] = None, **extra) -> dict`

A regenerative amplifier (1-D): ``round_trips`` = N or "auto" (eject at the energy maximum); ``cavity`` = {"lossPerRoundTrip": .., "gddFs2": .., "todFs3": .., "materials": [...]}.

### `saturable_absorber(id: str, kind: str = 'slow', modulation_depth: float = 0.02, nonsaturable_loss: float = 0.0, recovery_time_s: Optional[float] = None, saturation_fluence_j_per_m2: Optional[float] = None, spot_radius_m: Optional[float] = None, saturation_energy_j: Optional[float] = None, saturation_power_w: Optional[float] = None, kappa_per_w: Optional[float] = None) -> 'T.SaturableAbsorberElement'`

A saturable absorber element: kind "slow" (SESAM), "fast" or "kerrLens".

### `soft_aperture(id: str, radius_m: float, order: int = 1) -> dict`

A soft (Gaussian, or super-Gaussian of ``order``) aperture acting on a carried transverse profile.

### `gaussian_beam(w0_m: float, z_waist_m: float = 0.0, m2: float = 1.0, wavelength_m: Optional[float] = None) -> dict`

### `constant_beam(radius_m: Optional[float] = None, area_m2: Optional[float] = None) -> dict`

### `sampled_beam(z_m: Sequence[float], radius_m: Sequence[float]) -> dict`

### `material(index: Any = None, n2: Optional[float] = None, base: Optional[str] = None, raman: Any = None, attenuation: Any = None, gas: Optional[Mapping[str, Any]] = None, index_reference: Optional[str] = None, **extra) -> dict`

### `sellmeier(B: Sequence[float], C: Sequence[float]) -> dict`

### `gas(species: str, pressure_bar: float = 1.0, temperature_k: float = 293.15) -> dict`

### `coating_gdd(R: float, gdd_s2: float, tod_s3: float = 0.0) -> dict`

### `coating_quarter_wave(design: str, design_wavelength_m: float, H: str = 'Ta2O5', L: str = 'SiO2_film') -> dict`

### `pulse(center_wavelength_m: float, duration_fwhm_s: Optional[float] = None, energy: Optional[float] = None, shape: str = 'gaussian', rep_rate_hz: Optional[float] = None, average_power_w: Optional[float] = None, peak_power_w: Optional[float] = None, gdd_s2: float = 0.0, tod_s3: float = 0.0, polarization = 'x', **extra) -> 'T.Pulse'`

### `measured_spectrum(wavelengths_m: Sequence[float], intensity: Sequence[float], energy: Optional[float] = None, phase_rad: Optional[Sequence[float]] = None, *, background: Any = None, threshold: Optional[float] = None, resolution_m: Optional[float] = None, deconvolve: Optional[bool] = None, extrapolate: Optional[str] = None, center_wavelength_m: Optional[float] = None, **extra) -> 'T.Pulse'`

An input pulse from a measured spectrum (intensity per unit wavelength, optional phase), docs/reference/measured-data.md.

### `measured_spectrum_csv(csv: str, energy: Optional[float] = None, *, wavelength_unit: Optional[str] = None, background: Any = None, threshold: Optional[float] = None, resolution_m: Optional[float] = None, deconvolve: Optional[bool] = None, extrapolate: Optional[str] = None, center_wavelength_m: Optional[float] = None, **extra) -> 'T.Pulse'`

An input pulse from a spectrum file (CSV: wavelength, intensity, optional phase in rad; ``wavelength_unit`` "nm" (default), "um" or "m"). Relative paths are resolved against the run file's folder. Same cleaning and options as :func:`measured_spectrum`.

### `measured(file: Optional[str] = None, *, values: Optional[Mapping[str, Any]] = None, sigma: Optional[float] = None, normalize: Optional[str] = None, background: Any = None, columns: Optional[Mapping[str, str]] = None, range_x: Optional[Sequence[float]] = None, x_unit: Optional[str] = None, y_unit: Optional[str] = None, value_sigma: Optional[float] = None, weight: Optional[float] = None, resolution_m: Optional[float] = None, resolution_s: Optional[float] = None, match_resolution: Optional[bool] = None, scale: Optional[str] = None, sigma_db: Optional[float] = None, floor_db: Optional[float] = None, simulated: Optional[Mapping[str, str]] = None, **extra) -> 'T.Measured'`

Recorded data for an instrument (its ``measured`` key; docs/reference/measured-data.md): a CSV / NPZ / JSON ``file`` and/or scalar ``values`` ({name: value | [value, sigma]}, e.g. ``{"energyJ": [1.2e-6, 2e-8]}``).

### `instrument(kind: str, at: str = 'end', name: Optional[str] = None, **params) -> dict`

An instrument (docs/reference/instruments.md). Keyword arguments are its parameters in the engine's names (``resolutionM=...``, ``axis=axis(...)``, ``detector={...}``, ``measured=measured(...)`` to compare with a recording).

### `axis(values: Optional[Sequence[float]] = None, *, start: Optional[float] = None, stop: Optional[float] = None, step: Optional[float] = None, points: Optional[int] = None, bin_width: Any = None, resolution: Optional[float] = None) -> dict`

Where a curve instrument takes its readings (docs/reference/instruments.md#axis-where-readings-are-taken): explicit ``values`` (e.g. your spectrometer's pixel wavelengths) or ``start``/``stop`` with ``step`` or ``points``, each reading integrating over ``bin_width`` (a number or "pixel") and blurred by a Gaussian ``resolution`` (FWHM). SI units of the axis (m for wavelengths, s for delays). Use as ``instrument("spectrometer", axis=axis(...))``.

### `override(target: str, prop: str, model: Any = None, value: Any = None, mode: str = 'replace') -> dict`

### `physics(*, beam_tracking: Any = None, spatio_temporal: Any = None, transverse: Optional[Mapping[str, Any]] = None, **extra) -> 'T.Physics'`

Physics switches of a run (``run_spec(physics=...)``). ``beam_tracking``: "auto" | "on" | "off" (Gaussian q tracking from the ``input_beam``); ``spatio_temporal``: "auto" | "on" | "track" | "off" -- angular / spatial dispersion and pulse-front tilt carried with the tracked beam, their group-delay dispersion applied to the pulse ("track": reported only); ``transverse``: the default spatial model. Other keys (``nonlinear``, ``raman``, ...) go through ``extra``.

### `run_spec(pulse: Mapping[str, Any], name: str = 'run', grid: Optional[Mapping[str, Any]] = None, physics: Optional[Mapping[str, Any]] = None, stepper: Optional[Mapping[str, Any]] = None, probes: Any = 'all', instruments: Optional[list] = None, overrides: Optional[list] = None, outputs: Optional[Mapping[str, Any]] = None, input_beam: Optional[Mapping[str, Any]] = None, compute: Optional[Mapping[str, Any]] = None, detectors: Optional[Mapping[str, Any]] = None, **extra) -> 'T.RunSpec'`

A run spec. ``compute`` selects the compute back-end (:func:`compute`; GPU: ``compute(backend="auto")``). ``extra`` adds top-level keys provided by plugins, e.g. ``fit=`` (fitting plugin: ``from ultrafast_fitting import fit``).

### `compute(backend: Optional[str] = None, *, threads: Optional[int] = None, fft: Optional[str] = None, device: Optional[int] = None, gpu_min_points: Optional[int] = None) -> 'T.Compute'`

Where the run computes (docs/reference/speed.md).

### `sampling(plane: str = 'near', aperture: str = 'pinhole', radius_m: Optional[float] = None, width_m: Optional[float] = None, focal_length_m: Optional[float] = None, center_x_m: Optional[float] = None, center_y_m: Optional[float] = None, na: Optional[float] = None, propagate_m: Optional[float] = None) -> dict`

Where an instrument looks (docs/reference/instruments.md): ``plane`` "near" | "far" (focal plane of a lens of ``focal_length_m``), ``aperture`` "integrated" | "pinhole" | "iris" | "fibre" | "slit" | "point". Use as ``instrument("spectrometer", sampling=sampling("far", "fibre", radius_m=25e-6, focal_length_m=0.1))``.

### `save(obj: Mapping[str, Any], path: str) -> str`

## `ultrafast.measured`

Measured data: typed comparisons of instruments with recordings (`res.comparisons`), compared arrays.

Measured data: recordings compared with the simulated instruments, and typed access to the comparisons.

### class `ComparedValue(TypedDict)`

One scalar reading compared with its recorded value.


### class `Comparison(TypedDict)`

An instrument compared with recorded data (one entry of ``summary["comparisons"]``).


### class `MeasuredCurve(TypedDict)`

A compared curve on the measured axis (SI units), normalised as in the comparison.


### class `MeasuredTrace(TypedDict)`

A compared 2-D trace on the measured axes, [rows, cols].


### `comparisons(result: Any) -> List[Comparison]`

Every instrument compared with recorded data (a :class:`ultrafast.Result` or a results folder), or [].

### `comparison(result: Any, instrument: str) -> Comparison`

The comparison of one instrument (by name). KeyError if it has none.

### `total_chi2(result: Any) -> float`

Sum of the chi^2 of all comparisons (``summary["measuredChi2"]``), 0 if none.

### `curve(result: Any, instrument: str) -> MeasuredCurve`

The measured curve and the simulated reading on the same (measured) axis, as compared.

### `trace(result: Any, instrument: str) -> MeasuredTrace`

The measured 2-D trace and the simulated trace on the same axes, as compared ([rows, cols]).

Names of everything the engine knows: built-in materials, gases, birefringent crystals, refractiveindex.info pages.

### `show(name: str) -> Dict[str, Any]`

Index model, n2, rotational Raman and a table of n, group index and GVD (fs^2/mm) of a material or page.

### `import_page(path: 'os.PathLike[str] | str', name: Optional[str] = None) -> Dict[str, Any]`

Copy a refractiveindex.info YAML page into the user library and return the material definition to use.

An index model dict for a refractiveindex.info page (bundled, imported, a file, or from ULTRAFAST_RII_PATH).

## `ultrafast.laser`

Laser and amplifier helpers.

Building mode-locked oscillators (docs/reference/oscillators.md).

### class `Oscillator`

Fluent builder for an ``oscillator`` element (models "haus", "cavity", "parametric").

* `__init__(id: str = 'laser', model: str = 'haus', rep_rate_hz: Optional[float] = None, cavity_length_m: Optional[float] = None, ring: bool = False, output_coupler: float = 0.05)`
* `simple_gain(small_signal_gain: float, saturation_energy_j: Optional[float] = None, saturation_power_w: Optional[float] = None, bandwidth_m: Optional[float] = None, center_wavelength_m: Optional[float] = None, shape: str = 'lorentzian', fluence_saturation_energy_j: Optional[float] = None) -> 'Oscillator'` -- Lumped gain: power gain per round trip ``small_signal_gain``, saturated by the intracavity pulse energy (or average power), spectral shape of FWHM ``bandwidth_m``.
* `gain_medium(medium: Any, length_m: float, pump: dict, mode_radius_m: float, passes: int = 2, slices: int = 8, relaxation: float = 0.2, **extra) -> 'Oscillator'` -- A real gain medium (cavity model): cw pump, inversion from the average powers, spectral gain, host dispersion and SPM on every pass.
* `loss(fraction: float) -> 'Oscillator'`
* `dispersion(gdd_fs2: float = 0.0, tod_fs3: float = 0.0) -> 'Oscillator'`
* `spm(rad_per_w: float) -> 'Oscillator'` -- Self-phase modulation per round trip: phase = rad_per_w x power.
* `absorber(kind: str = 'slow', **params) -> 'Oscillator'` -- Saturable absorber: haus model -> the lumped absorber; cavity model -> a saturableAbsorber element appended to the cavity. Parameters as in docs: modulation_depth, nonsaturable_loss, recovery_time_s, saturation_fluence_j_per_m2 + spot_radius_m (or saturation_energy_j), saturation_power_w, kappa_per_w.
* `add(*elements) -> 'Oscillator'` -- Append engine elements (as built with ultrafast.build) to the cavity round trip, in order.
* `start(mode: str = 'noise', seed_energy_j: Optional[float] = None, seed: Optional[int] = None) -> 'Oscillator'`
* `round_trips(max: int = 5000, tolerance: float = 1e-05, check_every: int = 25, snapshots: int = 120) -> 'Oscillator'`
* `element() -> dict`
* `system(name: Optional[str] = None, after: Optional[List[dict]] = None) -> dict` -- A system file: the oscillator, then optionally ``after`` (e.g. a compressor, an amplifier).
* `soliton_fwhm_s(gdd_s2: float, spm_rad_per_w: float, energy_j: float) -> float` -- Soliton area theorem: FWHM = 3.53 |GDD| / (delta E) (sech^2 pulse, lumped cavity).
* `kerr_spm_coefficient(n2: float, length_m: float, mode_radius_m: float, wavelength_m: float, passes: int = 2) -> float` -- delta (rad/W) of a Kerr medium: k0 n2 L passes / (pi w^2 / 2).

## `ultrafast.crystal`

χ(2) crystal helpers.

Phase-matching calculator (the engine's ``PhaseMatchCalculator``, also ``ultrafast crystal`` on the CLI).

### `crystals() -> list`

Names of the built-in chi(2) crystals.

### `phase_match(crystal: Union[str, dict], process: str = 'shg', type: Optional[str] = None, *, fundamental: Optional[float] = None, pump: Optional[float] = None, signal: Optional[float] = None, idler: Optional[float] = None, a: Optional[float] = None, b: Optional[float] = None, plane: Optional[str] = None, theta_deg: Optional[float] = None, phi_deg: Optional[float] = None, noncollinear: Union[None, float, str] = None, qpm: Union[None, bool, float] = None, length: float = 0.001, temperature_c: Optional[float] = None, pump_intensity: Optional[float] = None, polarizations: Optional[Dict[str, str]] = None, **extra) -> dict`

Solve phase matching. Wavelengths in metres; ``noncollinear`` in degrees or ``"magic"``; ``qpm=True`` (period found) or a period in metres. ``type`` defaults to "I" (birefringent) or "0" (QPM). Returns the calculator's JSON as a dict with ``phaseMatched``, ``best`` (angles, deffPmPerV, waves, acceptance, gvm, gainSpectrum...) and ``solutions``.

Quick plots of results (matplotlib).

Plot results written by the ``ultrafast`` CLI.

## `ultrafast.plotting`

Plot helpers used by `plot`.

Publication-style plots of UltrafastEngine results (needs matplotlib: ``pip install ultrafast-engine[plot]``).

### `set_theme(dark: bool = False) -> None`

Switch the colour theme for figures created afterwards.

### class `SavedResult`

A results folder written by the CLI / ``Result.write``: same interface as a live Result (``summary``, ``provenance``, ``names()``, ``result[name]``, ``instrument(name)``, ``comparisons``, ``comparison(name)``).

* `__init__(directory: Union[str, Path])`
* `name() -> str`
* `names() -> List[str]`
* `instrument(name: str) -> dict`
* `comparisons()` -- Instruments compared with recorded data (:mod:`ultrafast.measured`).
* `comparison(instrument: str)` -- The comparison of one instrument with its recorded data (KeyError if it has none).

### `load(source) -> 'SavedResult'`

A results folder (str/Path) -> :class:`SavedResult`; a live Result / SavedResult is returned as is.

### `fmt(x, unit: str = '', digits: int = 3) -> str`

Engineering formatting: fmt(2.2e-13, 's') -> '220 fs'.

### `temporal(res, ax = None, compressed: bool = True, normalize: bool = False)`

Input and output power vs time (plus the ideally compressed output, if an ideal compressor ran).

### `spectrum(res, ax = None, db: bool = False, floor_db: Optional[float] = None)`

Input and output spectral density vs wavelength (linear, normalised; or dB). With ``db``, the floor follows the data (down to -120 dB) unless ``floor_db`` is given, and the wavelength range covers everything above it.

### `spectral_phase(res, ax = None, xlim = None)`

Output (and input) spectral phase with offset and group delay removed, where the spectrum is > 1 %.

### `evolution(res, axs = None)`

Energy, FWHM and cumulative B-integral after each element (three stacked panels, shared x).

### `losses(res, ax = None)`

Energy budget by mechanism. Losses are positive; energy brought in by auxiliary beams (crystals, amplifiers) is negative ("from pump (aux)"). Shown as % of all energy that entered (input + auxiliary beams).

### `key_numbers(res, ax = None)`

Text panel with the headline numbers, warnings and notes.

### `overview(res, db: bool = False)`

Six-panel summary: pulse, spectrum, spectral phase, evolution, losses, key numbers.

### `system_diagram(res, ax = None, compact: bool = False)`

Schematic of the system on ``ax``: elements, beam line coloured by carrier wavelength, aux beams in, by-products out, probes and numbered instrument locations (the numbers used in every instrument title).

### `system(res)`

Stand-alone system schematic with a numbered list of the instruments and where they sit.

### `instruments(res)`

One panel per instrument (d-scan / FROG traces as images). Returns None if no instrument has data.

### `probes(res, db: bool = True, floor_db: Optional[float] = None)`

Spectral and temporal evolution through the probes (heat maps, one row per probe, input at the bottom). The dB floor follows the data (down to -60 dB) unless ``floor_db`` is given. Returns None if the run recorded fewer than two probes.

### `elements(res)`

Per-element quantities as small multiples (shared x = element).

### `compare(results: Sequence, labels: Optional[Sequence[str]] = None, db: bool = False)`

Overlay the output pulse and spectrum of several runs (max. 8; colours follow the run order).

### `byproducts(res)`

Fields that left an active element alongside the main beam (crystal idler / unconverted pump, ...): one row per element, spectrum and power of the main output and of every recorded by-product. Returns None if the run has none.

### `gain(res)`

Gain and amplifier elements: one row per element with the single-pass small-signal gain spectrum (and the output spectrum), the inversion along the crystal before / after the pulse (or across the beam for spatial models), the build-up per pass / round trip and the pulse-train convergence. Returns None if the run has none.

### `oscillator(res)`

Oscillator elements: build-up of the output energy over the round trips, the evolution of the output pulse (time) and spectrum (wavelength) from start-up to steady state, and the final pulse with the key numbers. Returns None if the run has no iterated oscillator.

### `measurements(res)`

Recorded data against the simulation (instruments with ``measured`` data, docs/reference/measured-data.md): one row per instrument with "measured" data -- the measured curve (points), the simulated reading on the same axis (line, with its 1-sigma band after a fit) and the residual; for 2-D traces (FROG, d-scan, cameras) the measured and simulated traces and their difference; for scalar readings a table. Returns None if the run compared nothing.

### `register_figure(name: str, maker: Callable, after: Optional[str] = None) -> None`

Add a figure to :func:`report` and ``ultrafast-plot`` (used by plugins, e.g. the fitting plugin's ``measurements`` and ``fit``). ``maker(res)`` returns a matplotlib figure, or None when the result has no data for it. ``after`` places it after an existing figure in the default order.

### `report(res, out_dir: Union[str, Path, None] = None, formats: Iterable[str] = ('png',), pdf: bool = True, only: Optional[Iterable[str]] = None, db: bool = False, dpi: int = 160, close: bool = True) -> Dict[str, object]`

Draw every figure that has data, save them as ``<out_dir>/<name>.<fmt>`` and (optionally) all of them in one ``report.pdf``. ``out_dir`` defaults to ``<results folder>/plots``. Returns {name: figure or path}.

### `plot(result, what = 'overview', ax = None)`

``uf.plot(result, what)``: "overview" or "measurements" (figures), or a single panel "temporal" / "spectrum" / "phase" / "losses" / "elements" on ``ax``.

## `ultrafast.diagram`

Layout diagrams of a system.

Schematic of a simulated system for the plots: elements in order, the beam line coloured by its carrier wavelength, auxiliary beams coming in, by-products leaving, probes, and numbered instrument locations.

### `circled(n: int) -> str`

### `instrument_locations(summary: dict) -> List[dict]`

Instruments in system order (input first, then by element, end last), numbered from 1. Each entry: number, tag (①), name, kind, at, index (-1 input, element index, len for end), where, virtual.

### `location_text(summary: dict, at: str) -> str`

### `wavelength_color(lam: float) -> str`

Approximate perceived colour of a wavelength; IR fades from deep red to grey-brown, UV to violet-grey.

### `group_elements(els: List[dict], max_items: int = 22) -> List[dict]`

Collapse repeated units (e.g. 20 x [pass, mirror] in a multipass cell) into one item with a repeat count. Returns items {"start": i, "unit": L, "repeat": R}; plain elements have unit 1, repeat 1.

### `draw_system(res, ax, theme: dict, compact: bool = False)`

Draw the schematic of ``res`` (live Result or results folder) on ``ax``.
